description_good_justification: README.md line 3 gives a succinct one-line description: 'C2PA manifest embedding, referencing, and hard binding for HTML documents.' Cargo.toml 'description' field matches.
interact_justification: README.md documents install via crates.io/npm/PyPI (lines 22-33), links to Security reporting (line 202) and License (204-206). CONTRIBUTING.md explains fork/branch/PR workflow. Issues are open at https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-html/issues (gh api confirms has_issues=true).
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md 'Submitting Changes' section: fork, branch from main, add tests, run cargo test/clippy/fmt, open a PR (lines 27-33).
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md specifies acceptance requirements: cargo test --all-features, cargo clippy --all-features -- -D warnings, cargo fmt --all -- --check, and Conventional Commits style (lines 30-37).
floss_license_justification: Cargo.toml: license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"; dual-licensed under LICENSE-MIT and LICENSE-APACHE at repo root, both OSI-approved FLOSS licenses.
floss_license_osi_justification: Both MIT (LICENSE-MIT) and Apache License 2.0 (LICENSE-APACHE) are OSI-approved licenses; user may choose either per README.md line 206.
license_location_justification: LICENSE-APACHE and LICENSE-MIT hold the full texts (dual MIT OR Apache-2.0 per Cargo.toml); a top-level LICENSE file (identical to LICENSE-APACHE) is also present at the repository root for tooling that only recognizes that exact filename.
documentation_basics_justification: README.md provides overview, usage examples (embed/extract/remove, hard binding), and links; crate also publishes docs.rs API reference (badge in README.md line 7, package.metadata.docs.rs in Cargo.toml).
documentation_interface_justification: Public API (document::embed/embed_reference/extract/remove, hardbinding::compute_data_hash/verify_data_hash) is documented via rustdoc (#![warn(missing_docs)] in src/lib.rs:95 enforces doc coverage) and published at docs.rs/c2pa-html.
sites_https_justification: Repository is served at https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-html; crates.io, docs.rs, npmjs.com, and PyPI (all linked/referenced in README.md) are HTTPS-only.
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues is enabled and public (gh api repos/writerslogic/c2pa-html --jq '.has_issues' returns true) at https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-html/issues, searchable, URL-addressable, open to any GitHub user, no proprietary client required. GitHub Discussions is disabled (has_discussions=false) but Issues alone satisfies this criterion.
english_justification: All documentation (README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) and code comments are in English.
maintained_justification: git log shows 15 commits between 2026-07-30 and 2026-08-22 (most recent: 494958c, 2026-08-22), including active dependency and security maintenance (dependabot PRs #1-#5 merged, 8249f36 'bump pyo3 to 0.29' for a security fix). Repo is under 1 month old but shows continuous activity through the present.
repo_public_justification: Public GitHub repository at https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-html (gh api confirms isPrivate=false); full git history readable without authentication.
repo_track_justification: git (via GitHub) records every commit's author, timestamp, and diff; e.g. 'git log' shows author David Condrey <davidcondrey@me.com> and dependabot[bot] with full commit messages and dates.
repo_interim_justification: git log shows commits between the v0.1.0 and v0.2.0 tags (e.g. 89d01ad 'feat: add WebAssembly bindings and an npm release job', 472d7c0, 07efb37), not only tagged release commits.
repo_distributed_justification: Repository uses git, a distributed version control system, hosted on GitHub.
version_unique_justification: Cargo.toml version = "0.2.0"; git tags v0.1.0 and v0.2.0 each map to a unique commit and are published as unique crates.io/npm/PyPI package versions.
version_semver_justification: Versions 0.1.0 and 0.2.0 (git tag output) follow Semantic Versioning MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH format, matching Cargo.toml's version field.
version_tags_justification: git tag lists v0.1.0 and v0.2.0; both correspond to published GitHub Releases (gh release list shows v0.1.0 2026-07-31, v0.2.0 2026-08-02).
release_notes_justification: gh release view v0.1.0 and v0.2.0 show release bodies containing only an auto-generated 'Full Changelog: <compare-URL>' link (raw commit-range diff), not a curated human-readable summary of changes. cliff.toml (git-cliff Keep-a-Changelog config) exists at repo root but no CHANGELOG.md has been committed and no release body includes cliff-generated notes. Not N/A: the crate ships discrete versioned releases to crates.io, npm, and PyPI intended for external reuse.
release_notes_vulns_justification: N/A because release_notes itself is Unmet (no curated release notes exist yet to identify fixed vulnerabilities in). No publicly disclosed CVE/vulnerability has been fixed in this project's history to date.
report_process_justification: GitHub Issues is enabled with structured templates at .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml and feature_request.yml, and .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml; CONTRIBUTING.md 'Reporting Issues' section (lines 11-14) documents the process.
report_tracker_justification: GitHub Issues (per-issue tracker) is used, with dedicated bug_report.yml and feature_request.yml templates under .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/.
report_responses_justification: No qualifying reports exist to assess a majority against (evidence: gh issue list -R writerslogic/c2pa-html --state all --limit 20 returns zero issues (open or closed) as of 2026-08-26. With no bug reports filed in the project's ~4-week history, there is no unacknowledged report, so the criterion is vacuously satisfied.). Marked unknown rather than asserting a vacuous Met — flag for maintainer confirmation if/when real reports arrive.
enhancement_responses_justification: No qualifying enhancement requests exist to assess a majority against (evidence: gh issue list -R writerslogic/c2pa-html --state all --limit 20 returns zero issues of any kind, including enhancement requests. No enhancement request has gone without a response because none has been filed.). Marked unknown rather than asserting a vacuous Met.
report_archive_justification: GitHub Issues at https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-html/issues is a publicly readable, searchable, permanent archive of any reports and responses (currently empty, but the mechanism exists and is public per gh api has_issues=true).
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md documents the process: private GitHub Security Advisory or email admin@writerslogic.com (lines 7-13), linked from README.md 'Security' section (line 202). Note: SECURITY.md line 12 links to 'github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-zip/security/advisories/new' (a sibling repo, not c2pa-html) -- likely copied from a template and not yet updated for this repo -- but the GitHub Security Advisories mechanism and the email fallback both remain valid reporting channels.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: SECURITY.md documents two private channels: a GitHub Security Advisory (private until published) and direct email to admin@writerslogic.com (lines 11-13).
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: N/A: no vulnerability reports have been received in the last 6 months (repo is ~4 weeks old, gh issue list shows zero issues, and no security advisories exist for this repo).
build_justification: Standard Cargo build: `cargo build` (Cargo.toml, README.md line 23-25 shows dependency usage; CONTRIBUTING.md line 23 documents `cargo build`). CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs `cargo check`, `cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
build_common_tools_justification: Uses Cargo, the standard Rust build tool, plus maturin/PyO3 for the Python wheel and wasm-bindgen/wasm-pack for the npm package (README.md lines 28-33, Cargo.toml [package.metadata.docs.rs] and pyo3 dependency) -- all standard, common tools for their respective language ecosystems.
build_floss_tools_justification: Cargo, rustc, maturin/PyO3, and wasm-bindgen are all FLOSS. Cargo.toml shows zero non-optional dependencies ('Zero dependencies, no features', README.md line 166-170).
test_invocation_justification: `cargo test` is the standard Rust test invocation (CONTRIBUTING.md line 24, ci.yml 'test' job runs `cargo test`); documented in CONTRIBUTING.md Development Setup.
test_justification: 103 #[test] functions across src/base64.rs, src/document.rs, src/error.rs, src/hardbinding.rs, src/scan.rs, src/sha2.rs, and tests/roundtrip.rs (grep -c '#[test]' counts: 7+31+7+23+17+10+8). Run via `cargo test`, documented in CONTRIBUTING.md lines 20-25. All FLOSS (MIT/Apache-2.0, same as the crate).
test_most_justification: Core logic (discovery/scan, document embed/extract/remove, base64, hard-binding hash/verify, SHA-2 against NIST FIPS 180-4 vectors, error paths) is heavily tested: 103 test functions in src/*.rs and tests/roundtrip.rs. Gap: src/wasm.rs and src/python.rs (FFI binding layers) have zero #[test] functions (grep -c '#[test]' src/wasm.rs src/python.rs returns 0/0) -- only the core Rust API is directly unit-tested, not the WASM/Python surface.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: .github/workflows/ci.yml 'test' job runs `cargo test` on every push to main and every pull request (paths-ignore markdown-only changes).
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md line 30: 'Make changes, add tests, run `cargo test --all-features`' is an explicit stated policy that new changes include tests.
tests_are_added_justification: Policy is inconsistently followed: commit 4da0ea2 'feat: C2PA manifest embedding and hard binding for HTML documents' (the core feature) added substantial tests in src/document.rs and src/hardbinding.rs. But commit 89d01ad 'feat: add WebAssembly bindings and an npm release job' added src/wasm.rs with zero #[test] functions, and src/python.rs likewise has zero tests -- major functionality (the WASM and Python binding surfaces) shipped without accompanying tests.
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md 'Submitting Changes' step 2 explicitly documents the add-tests policy: 'Make changes, add tests, run `cargo test --all-features`' (line 30).
warnings_justification: src/lib.rs lines 95-96 set `#![warn(missing_docs)]` and `#![warn(missing_debug_implementations)]` crate-wide; CI runs `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy --features python -- -D warnings` (.github/workflows/ci.yml lines 39-40), and `cargo fmt --all -- --check`.
warnings_fixed_justification: CI treats clippy warnings as build failures via `-D warnings` (ci.yml lines 39-40), so no clippy warning can persist on main without breaking CI. Commit 4b85f74 'chore: harden lints, docs, and CI' shows active warning cleanup.
warnings_strict_justification: src/lib.rs:94 `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` is the strictest possible unsafe-code lint (hard compile error, stronger than deny/warn); combined with clippy -D warnings across all targets and the python feature, and rustfmt --check, this is a maximally strict practical warning configuration for this crate.
know_secure_design_justification: README.md explicitly documents secure-design reasoning for the crate's core function: hard-binding coverage semantics and why re-serialization invalidates a binding (lines 106-119), and a documented rationale for why SHA-2 is hand-rolled versus other crypto being out of scope (lines 172-180, 'A hash is the one primitive where writing it yourself is uncontroversial'). src/lib.rs:94 `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` and SECURITY.md's supply-chain section (pinned SHA actions, least-privilege GITHUB_TOKEN in 8827fcf) show deliberate secure-design practice by the primary developer.
know_common_errors_justification: SECURITY.md 'Supply-chain security' section documents specific mitigations for common attack classes (actions pinned to SHAs against tag-mutation attacks, Scorecard/Dependabot, minimal GITHUB_TOKEN permissions -- commit 8827fcf 'ci(security): pin actions by SHA and drop GITHUB_TOKEN to read'). Commit 8249f36 'fix(security): bump pyo3 to 0.29' shows responding to a known dependency vulnerability class.
crypto_published_justification: src/sha2.rs implements SHA-256/384/512 per the published FIPS 180-4 standard, tested against published NIST test vectors (README.md lines 172-175: 'implemented against FIPS 180-4 and tested against the NIST vectors').
crypto_call_justification: The crate deliberately reimplements SHA-2 in-crate (src/sha2.rs) rather than calling a dedicated crypto library, by design, to keep zero dependencies (README.md lines 166-180: 'Discovery, embedding, Base64, SHA-2, and the binding algorithm are all in-crate' / 'A hash is the one primitive where writing it yourself is uncontroversial'). This criterion is SHOULD-level and the project's own documented rationale (no key material, no timing side channel, fully pinned by public test vectors, and a pluggable Hasher trait for callers wanting an accelerated/vetted implementation) is a reasoned exception, but the literal criterion (call dedicated crypto software) is not met by default.
crypto_floss_justification: The in-crate SHA-2 implementation (src/sha2.rs) is itself FLOSS (MIT OR Apache-2.0, same as the whole crate), and callers may substitute any FLOSS implementation via the `Hasher` trait (README.md lines 178-180).
crypto_keylength_justification: N/A: the crate has no cryptographic keys of its own (hashing only, no signing/encryption/key-agreement); README.md lines 44-45 states 'Signature verification, certificate trust, assertion validation ... are not reimplemented here.'
crypto_working_justification: src/hardbinding.rs exposes only SHA-256/384/512 (Algorithm::Sha256/384/512 per README.md line 96-101); no MD4, MD5, single-DES, RC4, or Dual_EC_DRBG anywhere in the codebase (grep of src/ shows only the sha2 module).
crypto_weaknesses_justification: Only SHA-256/384/512 are offered as hard-binding digest algorithms (src/hardbinding.rs, src/sha2.rs); no SHA-1 or other weakened algorithm is used by default.
crypto_pfs_justification: N/A: the crate performs no key agreement or network key exchange; it is a local hashing/embedding library (README.md lines 39-45).
crypto_password_storage_justification: N/A: the crate has no concept of user accounts or stored passwords; it is an HTML document manipulation library.
crypto_random_justification: N/A: the crate generates no cryptographic keys or nonces and has zero dependencies including no RNG crate (Cargo.toml shows no rand/getrandom dependency); hashing is deterministic over caller-supplied bytes.
delivery_mitm_justification: Package is delivered via crates.io, npmjs.com, and PyPI (README.md lines 22-33), all served exclusively over HTTPS; source is fetched via `git clone https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-html.git` (CONTRIBUTING.md line 21, also HTTPS).
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hash-only integrity check is distributed over plain HTTP; all distribution channels (crates.io, npm, PyPI, GitHub over HTTPS) use TLS-protected transport, and README.md line 24 notes releases include build provenance where the registry supports it.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No publicly disclosed medium-or-higher vulnerability is currently open against this project (gh api shows no security advisories; gh issue list returns zero issues). Commit 8249f36 'fix(security): bump pyo3 to 0.29' (2026-08-04, same day as v0.2.0's predecessor commits) shows a dependency security fix applied promptly, well within 60 days.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No critical vulnerability has been publicly reported against this project to date (repo is ~4 weeks old with zero issues/advisories filed per gh issue list and gh api), so no case of slow response exists; the one dependency security fix observed (8249f36, pyo3 bump) landed the same day as related hardening work (4b85f74, 8827fcf), showing responsiveness.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: git log --all -p searched for api key/secret/password/private-key/token patterns found only legitimate GitHub Actions secret references (`${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}`, `${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}`, `${{ github.token }}` in .github/workflows/release.yml) and unrelated source matches (HTML 'token list' parsing in src/scan.rs, doc comments about there being 'no secret to leak' in a hash). No embedded credential, API key, or private key material found.
static_analysis_justification: clippy (a FLOSS static analysis tool for Rust) is run in CI on every push/PR: `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy --features python -- -D warnings` (.github/workflows/ci.yml lines 39-40, also in release.yml lines 52-54).
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: clippy's default lint set is primarily correctness/style-focused, not a dedicated vulnerability-pattern scanner. No cargo-audit, cargo-deny, or CodeQL *analysis* job exists in .github/workflows/ -- scorecard.yml only runs `github/codeql-action/upload-sarif` to publish the OpenSSF Scorecard's own SARIF output, it does not run CodeQL's semantic vulnerability analysis. SECURITY.md line 23 claims 'Dependency Review ... run in CI' but commit 70ba7e6 'ci: drop dependency-review' removed that job -- the SECURITY.md claim is stale.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: CI enforces `-D warnings` on clippy (ci.yml lines 39-40), so any clippy finding fails the build and must be fixed before merge; commit 4b85f74 'chore: harden lints, docs, and CI' shows active lint remediation.
static_analysis_often_justification: clippy runs in CI on every push to main and every pull request (.github/workflows/ci.yml triggers, lines 6-12), i.e. on every commit, not just before releases.
dynamic_analysis_justification: A cargo-fuzz target (fuzz/fuzz_targets/parse_untrusted.rs) drives the crate's untrusted-input parsers with libFuzzer; fuzz/README.md documents how to run it.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: N/A: src/lib.rs line 94 `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` makes any `unsafe` block a hard compile error; grep -rn 'unsafe' src/ confirms the only occurrence is that forbid attribute itself -- there is no memory-unsafe code to analyze.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The fuzz target builds with cargo-fuzz's default dev profile, which enables debug assertions and overflow checks, so Rust's integer-overflow and bounds checks act as assertions during fuzzing.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: N/A: no dynamic analysis tool is run (see dynamic_analysis, Unmet), so no medium+ dynamic-analysis findings exist to have been fixed.
